- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.75), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- If model shows a sharp spike in forecast followed by a steep drop, reduce subsequent forecast values by 1–3% to account for overreaction.
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–3 days (especially after spikes), apply a 1–2 day lag correction: shift forecast down by 0.5–1.5% per lag day.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” transitions, model tends to overcorrect; apply a dampening factor of 0.85 to forecast weights after sentiment reversal.
